records.title: Aspire Leaders Program (2027 Cohort 1)
records.overview: Free six-week online leadership programme for first-generation or limited-income university students and graduates aged 18 to 29. Applications for the 2027 programme close on 10 January 2027; Cohort 1 runs from 21 January to 4 March 2027.
records.program_dates: 2027 Cohort 1: 21 January to 4 March 2027 (programme page: 'Cohort 1 — 2027', 'January 21 – March 4', marked 'OPEN!')
records.deadline_text: Programme page: 'APPLICATIONS FOR THE 2027 ASPIRE LEADERS PROGRAM CLOSE JANUARY 10, 2027!' Home page: 'Applications for the 2027 Aspire Leaders Program are OPEN! Register your profile and fill out our application HERE before the January 10, 2027 deadline.' No time or time zone is stated. Cohort 4 — 2026 (October 21 – November 30) is marked 'Closed'.
funding_details: Programme page: 'A fully-funded program for emerging leaders.' and 'Free. No application fee. No tuition. No catch.'
Free certificate of completion; an optional verifiable e-credential bundle costs USD 5

Programme page lists graduate support: Skills Advancement Grants (up to USD 200), Community Action Award (up to USD 5,000), Seed Fund, Academic Advancement Grant and Conference Grant (amounts for the last three not stated)
application_process: Apply online before 10 January 2027 through the Apply button on aspireleaders.org; it leads to a registration page on engage.aspireleaders.org
The programme page says the application takes about 10 minutes: 'No essays. No recommendation letters. No cost.'
Eligibility is self-identified; no documentation is required
records.eligibility_reason: The 18-29 age range overlaps the profile's under-30 band (exact age not recorded), and a 2024 bachelor's graduate meets the 'enrolled in or graduated from a university program' rule. The programme is reserved for first-generation or limited-income students and graduates (self-identified), which the profile does not record. It is open to students and graduates 'around the world' with no country list, so the DRC is not excluded.
potential_issues: Applications for 2027 close on 10 January 2027; no time or time zone is given
Reserved for first-generation or limited-income applicants (self-identified)
Age limit 18 to 29; the date on which age is counted is not stated
Live sessions need a reliable internet connection

records.overview: Subsidised internships of up to six months for young graduates in the Political, Press and Information section of the EU Delegation in Kinshasa. The section follows diplomatic relations between the EU and the DRC and makes the EU's actions in support of the country's development known. The EEAS lists seven calls since February 2022, published at irregular intervals and open 7 to 16 days each. The latest call, for two internships in 2026 with provisional starts in March and October, closed on 25 January 2026.
records.program_dates: Up to six months. Provisional starts in the calls read: April 2022, November 2022, May 2023, April 2024, November 2024, May 2025, and March and October 2026.
records.expected_next_cycle: Irregular, one or two calls a year. The EEAS vacancies list of the EU Delegation in Kinshasa (read 19 November 2026) shows seven calls for this internship, with deadlines 24/02/2022, 09/10/2022, 31/03/2023, 2 February 2024, 26 September 2024, 18.04.2025 and 25 January 2026. Each call page read was published 7 to 16 days before its deadline (11.02.2022, 26.09.2022, 15.03.2023, 24.01.2024, 17.09.2024, 11.04.2025 and 15.01.2026). No call after 25 January 2026 is listed.
eligibility: Currently residing in the DRC or near Kinshasa: 'seuls les candidats résidant actuellement en République démocratique du Congo ou à proximité de Kinshasa seront pris en compte' (given local health and security conditions)
University degree, preferably in political science, international relations, humanities, or information and communication sciences (the 2025 call required a degree 'validé' in these fields)
No more than one year of professional experience after obtaining the degree, at the time the internship agreement is signed
Excellent French and good knowledge of English
Command of modern communication tools (especially social media) and of IT tools; excellent writing skills; basic knowledge of the EU and its action in the DRC
Experience producing digital content and using photo and video software; experience in event organisation is an asset
The call asks applicants to read the general eligibility criteria for a subsidised internship (Article 8 of Decision ADMIN(2017)28)
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction is stated on the call; only candidates currently residing in the DRC or near Kinshasa are considered
records.experience_requirement: At most one year of professional experience after graduation when the internship agreement is signed; experience producing digital content and using photo and video software is asked for; event experience is an asset
records.language_requirement: Excellent French and good knowledge of English ('Excellente maitrise du français et bonne connaissance de l’anglais')
other_requirements: EU citizens must prove cover against pandemic risk and repatriation costs, and hold an entry visa or temporary residence permit where applicable
The internship can only be offered in line with local law and the law of the intern's country of origin

records.overview: Annual French-African Foundation programme for young leaders from Africa and France: two weeks of meetings, training and exchanges with public and private decision-makers, one week in France and one in an African country. Applicants must be 28 to 40 with at least five years of professional experience. Applications for the 2027 edition close on 16 December 2026 at 15:00 GMT.
records.program_dates: Two weeks: one in France and one in an African country (dates and host country of the 2027 edition not stated)
records.deadline_text: Young Leaders page: 'Édition 2027 du programme Young Leaders' / 'Candidatez avant le 16 décembre 2026 à 15H GMT' (English version: '2027 edition of the Young Leaders program' / 'Apply before December 16, 2026 at 3:00 PM GMT').
eligibility: Âge : avoir entre 28 et 40 ans (aged 28 to 40)
Langue : parler couramment anglais (fluent in English)

Expérience professionnelle : justifier d'au moins 5 années d'expérience professionnelle avec des compétences en leadership et un impact démontrables (at least five years of professional experience with demonstrable leadership skills and impact)
Vision : a clear wish to build bridges between African countries and France
Nationality of a country of the African continent, or French nationality
Selection by an independent high-level jury, renewed each year, on excellence, commitment and potential

records.overview: UCT's Mastercard Foundation Scholars Program funds citizens of African countries who face significant social and economic barriers, for a first bachelor's degree or an eligible taught postgraduate programme (a Health Sciences postgraduate diploma, an honours degree or a coursework master's). The 2027 intake is closed: postgraduate scholarship applications closed on 31 October 2026. A UCT academic application and an offer of admission are also required.
